questions.text:
Which of the following sentences are the statements ? Find the truth values of those sentences which are statements:
a) Kathmandu is the capital of Nepal.
b) Nepal exports oil.
c) 3 + 5 = 8
d) Where do you live ?
e) Understand logic.
f) Oh! how beautiful the scene is?
questions.source_solution:
a) The given sentence is a declarative sentence. So, it is a statement and its truth value is true (T).
b) The given sentence is a declarative sentence. So, it is a statement and its truth value is false (F).
c) The given sentence is a declarative sentence. So, it is a statement and truth value is true (T).
d) The given sentence is an interrogative sentence. So, it is not a statement.
e) The given sentence is an imperative sentence. So, it is not a statement.
f) The given sentence is an exclamatory sentence. So, it is not a statement.

questions.text:
Let $p$ : demand is increasing and $q$ : supply is decreasing.
Express each of the following statements into words:
a) $\sim p$
b) $\sim q$
c) $p \land q$
d) $p \lor q$
e) $\sim p \land q$
f) $p \lor \sim q$
g) $\sim p \land \sim q$
h) $\sim(p \land q)$
questions.source_solution:
a) $\sim p$: Demand is not increasing.
b) $\sim q$: Supply is not decreasing.
c) $p \land q$: Demand is increasing and supply is decreasing.
d) $p \lor q$: Demand is increasing or supply is decreasing.
e) $\sim p \land q$: Demand is not increasing and supply is decreasing.
f) $p \lor \sim q$: Demand is increasing or supply is not decreasing.
g) $\sim p \land \sim q$: Neither demand is increasing nor supply is decreasing.
h) $\sim(p \land q)$: It is false that demand is increasing and supply is decreasing.

questions.text:

a) $p$ : temperature is increasing, $q$ : length is expanding.
Temperature is increasing and length is expanding.
b) $p$ : pressure is decreasing, $q$ : Volume is increasing.
Pressure is decreasing or volume is increasing.
c) $p$ : demand is increasing, $q$ : price is increasing.
Neither demand is increasing nor price is decreasing [i.e. not increasing].
d) $p$ : Pradeep is bold, $q$ : Sandeep is handsome.
It is false that Pradeep is bold or Sandeep is handsome.
questions.source_solution:
a) $p \land q$
b) $p \lor q$
c) $(\sim p \land \sim q)$
d) $\sim(p \lor q)$

p & q & \sim p & (\sim p) \land q \\
\hline
T & T & F & F \\
T & F & F & F \\
F & T & T & T \\
F & F & T & F \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
If $p=T, q=F, r=T, s=F$, find truth values of:
a) $p \land q$
b) $p \lor (\sim q)$
c) $(\sim p) \land (\sim q)$
d) $q \lor (p \land s)$
e) $\sim(\sim p)$
f) $(p \lor q) \land (r \lor s)$
questions.source_solution:
a) $T \land F = \mathbf{F}$
b) $T \lor (\sim F) = T \lor T = \mathbf{T}$
c) $(\sim T) \land (\sim F) = F \land T = \mathbf{F}$
d) $F \lor (T \land F) = F \lor F = \mathbf{F}$
e) $\sim(\sim T) = \sim F = \mathbf{T}$
f) $(T \lor F) \land (T \lor F) = T \land T = \mathbf{T}$

questions.text:
Prove by truth table:
a) $p \land (\sim p) \equiv c$ (contradiction)
b) $(p \lor q) \equiv (q \lor p)$
c) $\sim[p \lor (\sim q)] \equiv (\sim p) \land q$
d) $\sim[(\sim p) \land q] \equiv p \lor (\sim q)$
questions.source_solution:
a) $p \land (\sim p)$ evaluates to all $F$ values ($F, F$), hence equivalent to contradiction $c$.
b) $(p \lor q)$ and $(q \lor p)$ both evaluate to $T, T, T, F$, hence equivalent.
c) $\sim[p \lor (\sim q)]$ and $(\sim p) \land q$ both evaluate to $F, F, T, F$, hence equivalent.
d) $\sim[(\sim p) \land q]$ and $p \lor (\sim q)$ both evaluate to $T, T, F, T$, hence equivalent.

questions.text:
Find the truth value and negation of each:
a) $3 + 2 = 5$ or $6$ is a multiple of $5$.
b) $8$ is a prime number and $4$ is even.
c) If $3 > 0$ then $4 + 6 = 10$.
d) If $2$ is odd or $3$ is a natural number then $2 + 3 = 8$.
e) If $2 \times 3 = 5 \implies 3 > 1$ then $6$ is even.
f) Triangle $ABC$ is right angled at $B \iff AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2$.
questions.source_solution:
a) Truth value: **T** ($T \lor F = T$). Negation: "$3 + 2 \ne 5$ and $6$ is not a multiple of $5$."
b) Truth value: **F** ($F \land T = F$). Negation: "$8$ is not a prime number or $4$ is odd."
c) Truth value: **T** ($T \implies T = T$). Negation: "$3 > 0$ and $4 + 6 \ne 10$."
d) Truth value: **F** ($T \implies F = F$). Negation: "$2$ is odd or $3$ is a natural number and $2 + 3 \ne 8$."
e) Truth value: **T** ($T \implies T = T$). Negation: "If $2 \times 3 = 5$, then $3 > 1$ and $6$ is odd."
f) Truth value: **T** ($T \iff T = T$). Negation: "$ABC$ is right angled at $B$ and $AB^2+BC^2 \ne AC^2$, or $ABC$ is not right angled at $B$ and $AB^2+BC^2=AC^2$."

questions.text:
For the statements:
a) If $3$ is a natural number then $1/3$ is a rational number.
b) $x^2 = 4$ whenever $x = 2$.
c) If the battery is low then the mobile does not work well.
Find i) antecedent & consequent, ii) converse, inverse & contrapositive, iii) negation.
questions.source_solution:
a) i) Antecedent: $3$ is a natural number; Consequent: $1/3$ is rational.
ii) Converse: If $1/3$ is rational then $3$ is natural.
Inverse: If $3$ is not natural then $1/3$ is not rational.
Contrapositive: If $1/3$ is not rational then $3$ is not natural.
iii) Negation: $3$ is natural and $1/3$ is not rational.

b) i) Antecedent: $x=2$; Consequent: $x^2=4$.
ii) Converse: If $x^2=4$ then $x=2$.
Inverse: If $x \ne 2$ then $x^2 \ne 4$.
Contrapositive: If $x^2 \ne 4$ then $x \ne 2$.
iii) Negation: $x=2$ and $x^2 \ne 4$.

c) i) Antecedent: Battery is low; Consequent: Mobile does not work well.
ii) Converse: If mobile does not work well, then battery is low.
Inverse: If battery is not low, then mobile works well.
Contrapositive: If mobile works well, then battery is not low.
iii) Negation: Battery is low and mobile works well.

questions.text:
Prove that:
a) $p \lor (\sim p \land q)$ is a tautology.
b) $(p \land q) \implies (p \lor q)$ is a tautology.
c) $\sim(p \lor q) \land q$ is a contradiction.
d) $(p \land q) \land \sim(p \lor q)$ is a contradiction.
e) $[\sim q \land (p \implies q)] \implies \sim p$ is a tautology.
f) $[(p \land q) \implies p] \implies (q \land \sim q)$ is a contradiction.
questions.source_solution:
a) Truth values for all 4 rows are $T, T, T, T \implies$ **Tautology**.
b) Truth values for all 4 rows are $T, T, T, T \implies$ **Tautology**.
c) Truth values for all 4 rows are $F, F, F, F \implies$ **Contradiction**.
d) Truth values for all 4 rows are $F, F, F, F \implies$ **Contradiction**.
e) Truth values for all 4 rows are $T, T, T, T \implies$ **Tautology**.
f) Truth values for all 4 rows are $F, F, F, F \implies$ **Contradiction**.

questions.text:
If $A \cap B = \phi$, prove that:
a) $A \subseteq \overline{B}$
b) $B \cap \overline{A} = B$
c) $A \cup \overline{B} = \overline{B}$
questions.source_solution:
Given $A \cap B = \phi$:
a) $x \in A \implies x \notin B \implies x \in \overline{B}$. Hence $A \subseteq \overline{B}$.
b) $B \cap \overline{A} = \{x : x \in B \text{ and } x \notin A\} = \{x : x \in B\} = B$.
c) $A \cup \overline{B} = \{x : x \in A \text{ or } x \in \overline{B}\} = \{x : x \notin B \text{ or } x \in \overline{B}\} = \overline{B}$.

questions.text:
If $A \subseteq B$, prove that:
a) $\overline{B} \subseteq \overline{A}$
b) $A \cup B = B$
c) $A \cap B = A$
questions.source_solution:
Given $A \subseteq B$:
a) $x \in \overline{B} \implies x \notin B \implies x \notin A \implies x \in \overline{A}$. Hence $\overline{B} \subseteq \overline{A}$.
b) $A \cup B = \{x : x \in A \text{ or } x \in B\} = \{x : x \in B\} = B$.
c) $A \cap B = \{x : x \in A \text{ and } x \in B\} = \{x : x \in A\} = A$.

questions.text:
If $A, B, C$ are subsets of universal set $U$, prove:
a) $A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$
b) $A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)$
questions.source_solution:
a) $x \in A \cup (B \cap C) \iff x \in A \lor (x \in B \land x \in C) \iff (x \in A \lor x \in B) \land (x \in A \lor x \in C) \iff x \in (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$.
b) $x \in A \cap (B \cup C) \iff x \in A \land (x \in B \lor x \in C) \iff (x \in A \land x \in B) \lor (x \in A \land x \in C) \iff x \in (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)$.

f) $[(p \land q) \implies p] \implies (q \land \sim q)$ is a contradiction.
questions.source_solution:
a) Truth values for all 4 rows are $T, T, T, T \implies$ **Tautology**.
b) Truth values for all 4 rows are $T, T, T, T \implies$ **Tautology**.
c) Truth values for all 4 rows are $F, F, F, F \implies$ **Contradiction**.
d) Truth values for all 4 rows are $F, F, F, F \implies$ **Contradiction**.
e) Truth values for all 4 rows are $T, T, T, T \implies$ **Tautology**.
f) Evaluates to $T \implies F = F, F, F, F \implies$ **Contradiction**.

questions.text:
If $A \cap B = \phi$, prove that:
a) $A \subseteq \overline{B}$
b) $B \cap \overline{A} = B$
c) $A \cup \overline{B} = \overline{B}$
questions.source_solution:
Given $A \cap B = \phi$:
a) $x \in A \implies x \notin B \implies x \in \overline{B}$. Hence $A \subseteq \overline{B}$.
b) $B \cap \overline{A} = \{x : x \in B \text{ and } x \notin A\} = \{x : x \in B\} = B$.
c) $A \cup \overline{B} = \{x : x \in A \text{ or } x \in \overline{B}\} = \{x : x \notin B \text{ or } x \in \overline{B}\} = \overline{B}$.

questions.text:
If $A \subseteq B$, prove that:
a) $\overline{B} \subseteq \overline{A}$
b) $A \cup B = B$
c) $A \cap B = A$
questions.source_solution:
Given $A \subseteq B$:
a) $x \in \overline{B} \implies x \notin B \implies x \notin A \implies x \in \overline{A}$. Hence $\overline{B} \subseteq \overline{A}$.
b) $A \cup B = \{x : x \in A \text{ or } x \in B\} = \{x : x \in B\} = B$.
c) $A \cap B = \{x : x \in A \text{ and } x \in B\} = \{x : x \in A\} = A$.

questions.text:

a) $B - A = B \cap \overline{A}$
b) $A - B = A \cap \overline{B}$
c) $A - \overline{B} = B - \overline{A}$
questions.source_solution:
a) $B - A = \{x : x \in B 	ext{ and } x 
otin A\} = \{x : x \in B 	ext{ and } x \in \overline{A}\} = B \cap \overline{A}$.
b) $A - B = \{x : x \in A 	ext{ and } x 
otin B\} = \{x : x \in A 	ext{ and } x \in \overline{B}\} = A \cap \overline{B}$.
c) $A - \overline{B} = \{x : x \in A 	ext{ and } x 
otin \overline{B}\} = \{x : x \in A 	ext{ and } x \in B\} = A \cap B = B - \overline{A}$.

questions.text:
If $A, B, C$ are subsets of $U$, prove:
a) $A \cup (B \cap C) = (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$
b) $A \cap (B \cup C) = (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)$
questions.source_solution:
a) $x \in A \cup (B \cap C) \iff x \in A \lor (x \in B \land x \in C) \iff (x \in A \lor x \in B) \land (x \in A \lor x \in C) \iff x \in (A \cup B) \cap (A \cup C)$.
b) $x \in A \cap (B \cup C) \iff x \in A \land (x \in B \lor x \in C) \iff (x \in A \land x \in B) \lor (x \in A \land x \in C) \iff x \in (A \cap B) \cup (A \cap C)$.

questions.text:
Find the truth value and negation of each:
a) $3 + 2 = 5$ or $6$ is a multiple of $5$.
b) $8$ is a prime number and $4$ is even.
c) If $3 > 0$ then $4 + 6 = 10$.
d) If $2$ is odd or $3$ is a natural number then $2 + 3 = 8$.
e) If $2 \times 3 = 5 \implies 3 > 1$ then $6$ is even.
f) Triangle $ABC$ is right angled at $B \iff AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2$.
questions.source_solution:
a) Truth value: **T**. Negation: "$3 + 2 \ne 5$ and $6$ is not a multiple of $5$."
b) Truth value: **F**. Negation: "$8$ is not prime or $4$ is odd."
c) Truth value: **T**. Negation: "$3 > 0$ and $4 + 6 \ne 10$."
d) Truth value: **F**. Negation: "$2$ is odd or $3$ is natural and $2 + 3 \ne 8$."
e) Truth value: **T**. Negation: "If $2 \times 3 = 5$, then $3 > 1$ and $6$ is odd."
f) Truth value: **T**. Negation: "$ABC$ is right angled at $B$ and $AB^2+BC^2 \ne AC^2$, or $ABC$ not right angled at $B$ and $AB^2+BC^2=AC^2$."

questions.text:
For the statements:
a) If $3$ is a natural number then $1/3$ is rational.
b) $x^2 = 4$ whenever $x = 2$.
c) If the battery is low then the mobile does not work well.
Find i) antecedent & consequent, ii) converse, inverse & contrapositive, iii) negation.
questions.source_solution:
a) i) Ant: $3$ is natural, Con: $1/3$ is rational.
ii) Conv: If $1/3$ is rational then $3$ is natural; Inv: If $3$ is not natural then $1/3$ is not rational; Contrap: If $1/3$ is not rational then $3$ is not natural.
iii) Neg: $3$ is natural and $1/3$ is not rational.

b) i) Ant: $x=2$, Con: $x^2=4$.
ii) Conv: If $x^2=4$ then $x=2$; Inv: If $x \ne 2$ then $x^2 \ne 4$; Contrap: If $x^2 \ne 4$ then $x \ne 2$.
iii) Neg: $x=2$ and $x^2 \ne 4$.

c) i) Ant: Battery low, Con: Mobile does not work well.
ii) Conv: If mobile doesn't work well then battery is low; Inv: If battery is not low then mobile works well; Contrap: If mobile works well then battery is not low.
iii) Neg: Battery is low and mobile works well.

e) $[\sim q \land (p \implies q)] \implies \sim p$ is a tautology.
